messages:
ajay: Heads-up — saw a regression in streamed responses after yesterday's kernel-router tweak. p50 per-token decode for short streams jumped from ~24ms to ~28-30ms. CPU on the driver host also spikes during partial-decode handoffs.

lina: Which tweak exactly? commit/hash? any flamegraphs or perf traces? :eyes:

ajay: commit b7f2c9a — changed selection rule to prefer attn_v2 for seq_len < 128 to speed up batch decode. Attached quick flame snippet (excerpt):

```
kernel_router -> attn_v2
  memcpy  42%  (handoff hot path)
  compute 39%
  launch  19%
```

robert: Interesting — I saw more stall time in partial-decode queue when attn_v2 is used for mixed workloads. KV cache hit-rate stayed ~99%, so not a cache miss issue. Seems like handoff memcpy and small-kernel launch overhead dominates.

tess: Might be interacting badly with our streaming batch hold timer. For streams we currently use batch_hold_ms=12 and token_budget_target=32. If kernel launch overhead increases, holding slightly longer sometimes amortizes launch cost, but that hurts tail for interactive users.

ajay: Quick experiment: lowered batch_hold_ms from 12 -> 6 on stream-priority queue and kept token_budget_target 32. Results: p50 improved to ~26ms, but p95 increased ~7% due to context switches (more tiny batches).

perf-bot: nightly/regression-check: streaming_short_streams.p50: +12% vs baseline, partial_decode_stalls: +9%. See CI run 2026-03-15T03:12Z -> https://ci/internal/regs/1762

ciara: Proposed triage steps: 1) revert attn_v2 decision for routes marked streaming (canary) 2) run microbench harness with synthetic prefixes (len 8/32/64) to repro launch overhead 3) add metric for memcpy bytes during kernel handoff and per-request memcpy latency.

robert: I'll kick off nvprof and custom harness against canary cluster (will attach trace). Command I use:

```
./tools/bench_streams --model small --seqs 8,32,64 --concurrency 64 --trace nvprof --out /tmp/trace.json
```

lina: Also instrument the continuous-batcher to emit: queued_time_ms, hold_time_ms, kernel_launch_latency_ms per batch. That will help correlate batch formation vs kernel overhead.

ajay: Agreed. I'm rolling a hotfix: kernel_router will fallback to attn_v1 for routes with is_streaming=true until we confirm attn_v2 micro-op pattern. Hotfix going to canary in 15m. I'll post metrics after 30m.

ciara: Don't forget to rerun the kv-cache eviction profiler — small batches may evict prefetched KV entries faster. Use `kvprof --window 30s` and add per-request KV lookup hist.

robert: will do. starting trace now.

lina: Thanks. If the reconnects/partial-decode stalls persist after the fallback, we should consider integrating a tiny gap-coalescer: hold micro-batches up to 4 tokens or 4ms to reduce kernel churn. Not a long-term fix but helps while we debug.

ajay: noted. Will monitor hotfix. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

perf-bot: autotest: canary-hotfix streaming_smoketest: PASS (p50 back within 3% of baseline)

robert: Trace uploaded: /tmp/trace_1862501234.nv.json — will annotate with memcpy hotspots.

ciara: leaving checklist here: revert-canary deployed, nvprof traces uploaded, batcher metrics added, kvprof run queued. Next sync in #eng-runtime in 2h.
